messages.content: The response should include at least 22 pronouns. how does trade impact on the pharaoh powers

message.content: Trade significantly strengthened the pharaoh's powers, and we can see this in many ways. The pharaoh, who ruled as a divine king, used their wealth from commerce to consolidate their authority. His armies were funded by the gold and grain that flowed through trade routes, so he could project power across the known world. The goods that they controlled—spices, timber, and precious stones—gave them leverage over vassal states. If a rival kingdom threatened Egypt, the pharaoh could cut off supply lines, and they would starve. It was a strategic advantage that no one could easily replicate. We should also note that the temples, which were extensions of the pharaoh's own will, benefited from trade revenues, and their priests reinforced the ruler's divine mandate. He, or she, in the rare cases of female pharaohs, wielded that economic power as a tool of both diplomacy and coercion. The subjects themselves understood that their livelihoods depended on the pharaoh's ability to maintain those trade networks, so their loyalty was, in many ways, economically compelled. It is clear that without trade, the pharaoh's power would have been far more limited than what the historical record shows us.
